objective: Audit recent activation history and frontier decisions to determine whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection produces better information flow.
bottleneck: Prior activations had durable conclusions but task choice was opportunistic from a queue.
question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
action: Audited the durable selector evidence without changing any process or controller code. Read LEARNING_STATE (frontier table + recent learning history), STATE activation records, state/campaign/task_queue.json, campaign_controller.py (task_rank + select_task), campaign_status.json, activation_status.json, and the runs directory. Distinguished two selector generations: (A) the worker-era frontier-first discipline recorded in LEARNING_STATE and (B) the new controller ordinal task_rank that assigned this campaign's tasks. Traced the 'no equivalent re-test' evidence to generation A, and established that generation B has zero completed-agent outcomes (this is agent 1 of the first campaign).
changed: state/campaign/runs/43523181606/agents/agent_01.json (this durable handoff record; no process/code/tooling change)
state/worker_progress.md (phase/milestone advanced to reflect the recorded process judgment)
verified: Inspected state/LEARNING_STATE.md lines 5-13 and 42-59: the frontier-first selection delta is recorded RETAIN(verified) with a clean ordering and six consecutive frontier cells (mean reversion 37263008074, cross-sectional relative strength 37304873966, volatility targeting 37314710995, momentum 37318950814, momentum lookback sweep 37361000967, longer-horizon momentum 37394344201, breakout 37414038601) each closed with a decisive, independently-verified verdict and no equivalent re-test.

Inspected state/LEARNING_STATE.md line 51: the opportunistic-queue baseline is documented (activation 37260572520 - 'the objective came from the queued receipt item rather than a frontier cell'; process-level delta UNVERIFIED), confirming the pre-delta comparison point.

Inspected .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py: the only selector is task_rank (lines 206-218) + candidate_tasks_for_role/select_task (lines 221-311); it is an ordinal qualitative ordering over (expected_information_gain, downstream_leverage, falsification_power, verifiability, effort, complexity, execution_risk, task_id), not a numeric reward score.

Verified the controller selected P-001 for agent 1 by that ranking: among the six OPEN LEARNING_PROCESS tasks (P-001..P-006), P-001 uniquely combines HIGH expected_information_gain, HIGH falsification_power and all-LOW cost, so it sorts first; this is consistent with the recorded selection_history in campaign_status.json (compared_against [P-001,P-002,P-004,P-003,P-006]).

Inspected state/campaign/runs/43523181606/campaign_status.json: completed_agents=[] and phase=AGENT_01_SELECTED; glob of state/campaign/runs/**/agents/agent_*.json returns only agent_01_contract.json and agent_01_before.json, i.e. this is the first campaign and the controller selector has zero completed-agent outcomes.

Inspected .github/scripts/validate_campaign_agent.py and evaluate_research_process.py to confirm this record conforms to controller schema (required fields, canonical decision/process_decision/task_selection_observation/failure_class values, list fields, single-line next, candidate_tasks passing validate_task).
unverified: The controller ordinal task_rank selector's own incremental effect on information flow: no campaign agent has completed under it yet (run 43523181606 is at agent 1 of 10), so no completed-agent outcome evidence exists; the durable support attaches to the worker-era frontier-first discipline, a different mechanism.

No quantitative counterfactual exists for the opportunistic-queue period; 'no equivalent re-tests' is attributed to the worker frontier-first discipline rather than directly to the controller's ordinal implementation, and the comparison is qualitative.

Borderline REGIME_STABLE verdicts in prior momentum/breakout cells sit near the framework's 0.05 noise band and remain threshold-sensitive (carried forward from prior activations; not re-tested in this audit).
observed_effect: Concrete evidence-backed finding: the frontier-first selection PRINCIPLE has durable support - six consecutive frontier cells were each closed with a decisive, independently-verified verdict and no equivalent re-test, versus the documented opportunistic-queue baseline where the process delta was UNVERIFIED. The controller ordinal task_rank faithfully formalizes that principle and selected a defensible highest-value task (P-001) for agent 1, but because this is the first campaign with zero completed agents, the controller selector's own incremental learning-efficiency benefit is NOT yet observed and must not be claimed as demonstrated. No equivalent re-test was found in the frontier table (the momentum lookback/horizon extensions carry new diagnostic purpose, permitted by learning rule 2). Campaign-liveness note (recorded, not acted on): only four OPEN HIGHER_ORDER_OBJECTIVE tasks exist (R-001,R-002,R-003,R-005; R-004 RESOLVED) for five even-agent slots, so a later even agent may find no OPEN task unless candidate_tasks supply one.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the current controller focused-task selector improves learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice.
uncertainty_reduced: Partially. The audit establishes that the durable 'cells closed without re-tests' evidence attaches to the frontier-first selection principle (worker-era), not yet to the controller's ordinal implementation; and that the controller selector has zero completed-agent evidence, so its incremental benefit cannot be asserted. This prevents the next agents from over-claiming the controller selector 'works' before campaign evidence exists and correctly attributes the durable support to the principle.
research_result: Process judgment (no market/research claim): retain the frontier-first selection discipline; classify the controller ordinal selector's incremental information-flow benefit as UNVERIFIED pending completed campaign-agent outcomes. No process, code, or tooling change was made.
next: After at least three campaign agents have completed, re-run this selector audit by comparing each controller-selected task against the frontier-first baseline (did it close a distinct unresolved cell without an equivalent re-test?) to convert the controller selector's effect from UNVERIFIED to a classified judgment.

candidate_tasks.primary_question: Do controller-selected tasks close distinct frontier cells without equivalent re-tests once at least three campaign agents have completed?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The controller ordinal selector's information-flow benefit is UNVERIFIED until completed campaign-agent outcomes exist.
candidate_tasks.objective: Compare completed controller-selected tasks against the frontier-first baseline to classify the controller selector's effect.
candidate_tasks.scope: Use completed agent_*.json records and the frontier/queue state only; no new experiments.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not modify controller code, add a numeric reward score, or start new research experiments.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A classified judgment (IMPROVED / UNCHANGED / WORSENED / UNVERIFIED) for the controller selector with per-agent evidence.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: Each completed agent is classified as closing a distinct cell without an equivalent re-test, or the shortfall is documented as UNVERIFIED.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop once at least three completed agent records are classified or the evidence is clearly insufficient.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side schema validation plus direct inspection of the cited agent_*.json and frontier records.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: P-001 established that the controller selector has zero completed-agent evidence at agent 1; this task supplies that evidence later in the campaign.

complexity_added: none (no process, code, or tooling change; only the durable handoff record and worker progress were written)
